parameters.content:
VIDEO VERSION — faithful reconstruction from the source evidence.
Source: https://www.instagram.com/rick_morty.tech/reel/Dainz37MOhU/
Evidence: [0.24s - 49.81s] [Speaker 0] Morty clogged code literally gets worse the longer you keep one single session running. Rick, you must be drunk. You just hit compact and it fixes everything, right? I am stone cold sober. Compacting does not always fix it. Even after you compact, it carries the shape of your old conversation forward, bad assumptions, dead ends, and messy debugging paths. All of that garbage leaks into the next part of your code. Then what do you actually do? What you actually want is a full handoff. Before you end the session, tell Claude to create a handoff dot MD file containing the goal, current current state, files it touched, what changed, what failed, and what it should do next. And then? Then you run slash clear or start a brand new Claude code session. You tell that new session to read the handoff file and continue exactly where the last one left off. So you're not dragging the whole mess into the new session? Good god. Exactly. You're giving a fresh agent a completely clean start. Comment anything positive down below, and I'll send you the full Claude code resources.
Source-vs-engineering boundary: MARVIN/NEXEN task ID, source citations, regression notes and a searchable append-only handoff index.
No external side effects are enabled on import.
